clue.text: Track restoration of Sacre Coeur

indicators.note: restoring a building reworks it, so the letters of the church's name are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Building work on the famous Paris basilica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restoration of' rearranges the letters of SACRE COEUR. Sacré-Cœur is the basilica on Montmartre in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-racing venue is a type of track, so the synonym fits.

clue.text: Tear grass

definitions.meaning: to tear is to dash along at speed
a marsh plant with hollow stems, used for chair seats

explanation.surface: Ripping up the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: hurrying along, and a waterside plant similar to a sedge.

clue.text: For a start, satisfaction in cryptic clues not infinite

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the scrambled group
cryptic means puzzling or obscure, signalling the letters of clues not are mixed up
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first of satisfaction is used

explanation.surface: A solver complaining that cryptic clues give endless satisfaction, or none at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' rearranges CLUES NOT, and 'in' places S, the start of 'satisfaction', within the scrambled letters. 'not infinite' looks like one phrase, but 'not' belongs to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too numerous to be totted up is effectively without limit, a synonym.

clue.text: Chicken wearing hat?

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat
if you have something on, you are wearing it

explanation.surface: A hen sporting headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: Wearing a hat is having a cap on, which gives the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cockerel fattened for the table is a kind of chicken.

clue.text: University books on drink, free

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sits on top of another, so these letters come first

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: A student who gets free booze after the library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down entry puts U plus NT above WINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unravel strands that were wound together is to free or disentangle them.

clue.text: Under lid of sparkly piano, view shiny disc

indicators.note: in a down entry, the next piece goes below the first two
in a down entry the lid is the top, so the first letter of sparkly is taken

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
an angle is a point of view

explanation.surface: Something glittering spotted beneath the lid of a sparkly piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' places ANGLE below S (top of 'sparkly') and P. 'lid' looks like the piano's lid but means the top of 'sparkly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glittering decoration sewn on clothes is a sequin, a shiny disc.

clue.text: Dairy product formed the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means back to front, so the word for formed is reversed

parts.note: something formed has been made

explanation.surface: Cheese or butter that was produced incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns MADE around.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch cheese with a red wax rind is an example of a dairy product.

clue.text: Exercise a bit on this?

definitions.meaning: military practice routine, as in parade-ground training
a power tool that bores holes holds a bit

explanation.surface: A suggestion to do a little exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' reads as 'a little', but it is the boring tip fitted to the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a training routine and a boring tool into which bits are fitted.

clue.text: Insignificant worker, one keeping going round the clock?

definitions.text: one keeping going round the clock?
definitions.note: a pointer that circles a clock face

parts.note: minute means tiny or trivial
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A lowly employee who works around the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round the clock' sounds like nonstop working, but the pointer literally goes round the clock face.
explanation.definitionFit: The longer pointer of a clock circles the dial continually, so it keeps going round.

clue.text: Tenant perhaps offering regular payment to save face

indicators.note: to save is to keep, so the payment word holds the other inside it

parts.note: rent is paid regularly to a landlord
a side is a face of a solid

explanation.surface: A lodger paying rent regularly to avoid losing face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to save' is a container signal: saving something means keeping it safe inside. 'face' is a side of a solid shape, not a person's face.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is one example of someone who lives in a place, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Puzzle remnant

definitions.meaning: what remains of a tree or a limb after cutting

explanation.surface: The leftover piece of a jigsaw.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both baffling someone and the stub left after something is cut down.

clue.text: Actor, terrible at reading

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so the letters of at reading are jumbled

explanation.surface: A performer who is awful at script reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges AT READING.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer specialising in tragic roles is a kind of actor.

clue.text: Smart clothes also showing status

indicators.note: to clothe is to wrap around, so the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: to smart is to sting
and means also

explanation.surface: Smart clothing as a sign of social rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb here, wrapping one piece around another. 'Smart clothes' reads as fine attire, but 'Smart' is the verb meaning to hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's rank or reputation in society is their position, a synonym of status.

clue.text: Bay allowed to trail in

indicators.note: to trail is to follow behind, so the word for allowed comes after in

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Permission for a ship to be towed into the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to trail' means to follow behind, so the word for 'allowed' comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: A small arm of the sea reaching into the land is a cove or bay.

clue.text: Engine's stable capacity?

parts.note: an engine's output is measured in units named after animals that live in stables

explanation.surface: How many animals the engine's stable can hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like 'steady', but it is the place horses are kept, so its capacity is counted in horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit measuring an engine's power is named for draught animals, so a stable's worth fits.

clue.text: Work in secret a reporter sent back

indicators.note: sent back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Undercover work for a journalist who sends in reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides ETAREPO in 'secret a reporter', and 'sent back' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: To function or run, as a machine does, is to work.

clue.text: Flower at the bottom of a fresh hole

indicators.note: in a down entry, the river is placed below the other pieces

parts.note: pert means cheeky, fresh
a river is a flower, something that flows; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A plant growing at the base of a new hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword trick for a river, here the Ure in Yorkshire; 'at the bottom of' places URE below A and PERT.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening or gap, such as in a camera lens, is a synonym for a hole.

clue.text: Remarkably easy, he having bagged fifty as batter?

indicators.note: to bag is to capture, so the scrambled letters surround the other piece
remarkably suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters of easy and he are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A cricketer scoring a half-century with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkably' signals the anagram and 'having bagged' the container. Fifty is a cricket score, but the batter here is something that bats: an eye blinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair on the eyelid moves when you bat your eyes, so it is a whimsical batter.

clue.text: Copy name and numbers in range

parts.note: to ape is to copy
nines are numbers

explanation.surface: Copying names and numbers into a list.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian mountain chain running down the peninsula is a range.

clue.text: Buried in waste, America put off

indicators.note: buried in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to spend is to use up or squander
US is America

explanation.surface: America buried in rubbish and postponing action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buried in' is the container signal. 'waste' looks like rubbish, but it is the verb meaning to squander.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer or postpone is to put off, a synonym.

clue.text: Two notes barely sufficient for singer

definitions.note: the definition is a melody, a part written for a singer

parts.note: D and E are musical notes
scant means barely enough

explanation.surface: Two notes are hardly enough for a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the part 'for singer': a counter-melody sung above the main tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative melody sung above the main tune is a part written for a singer.

clue.text: Plan talk ending in discussion

parts.note: patter is glib talk

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A plan for talk at the end of a discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending in' takes the N at the end of 'discussion'.
explanation.definitionFit: A template or design to follow is a plan.

clue.text: Family after shoe, orange leathery thing

indicators.note: after puts the family word behind the shoe

parts.note: a pump is a light shoe
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A family chasing a shoe made of orange leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the family word second. 'orange leathery' sounds like a shoe's material, but it is the tough rind of a squash.
explanation.definitionFit: The big orange squash with a tough skin fits a description of a leathery orange thing.

clue.text: Person flying towards brink, backwards

indicators.note: backwards says the two words together are read in reverse

parts.note: to means towards
a lip is an edge or brink

explanation.surface: Someone flying towards the edge and then back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns TOLIP around.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at the controls of an aircraft is a person flying it.

clue.text: Flower, third of fourteen in a large bunch

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the other word

parts.note: lots means a large number

indicators.note: the third letter of fourteen is taken

explanation.surface: One flower in fourteen, part of a big bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third of' takes U from 'fourteen'; 'in' puts it inside LOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred water lily of Asia is a flower.

clue.text: Short interval in game, no time seemingly for comeback?

indicators.note: for comeback says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A short break in a match that seemingly leaves no time for a team to fight back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides ENOTIMES in 'game, no time seemingly' and 'for comeback' turns it round. 'interval' suggests half-time, but it is a musical gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A half step between notes is the smallest interval in Western music.

clue.text: Transport minister's first item that's revered

parts.note: to tote is to carry

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of minister

explanation.surface: The transport minister's priority is a sacred object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives M, the start of 'minister's'. 'Transport minister' looks like a government post, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved emblem venerated by a clan is an object held sacred.

clue.text: Sad wife hugged by professor

indicators.note: being hugged means being held inside, so the wife letter goes within

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A miserable wife comforted by an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugged by' puts W inside DON; a don is a lecturer at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low or dejected is a synonym for sad.

clue.text: Faint design ends on hot pipe, boarding cosy old ship

indicators.note: boarding means getting on board, so those letters go inside the next word

parts.note: warm means cosy

indicators.note: the ends of words are their final letters, so the last letters of hot and pipe are taken

parts.note: Noah's ark is an ancient ship

explanation.surface: A faint design on a hot pipe inside a cosy old ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends on' takes T and E, the last letters of 'hot' and 'pipe'; 'boarding' puts them inside the word for cosy.
explanation.definitionFit: The faint image pressed into paper, seen when held to light, is a faint design.

clue.text: Dance beat has energy

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A dance whose beat has energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like the musical rhythm, but it means to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine ballroom dance is a type of dance.

clue.text: River and powdered lava in eruption

parts.note: volcanic ash is powdered lava

explanation.surface: A river and volcanic ash during a volcanic eruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eruption' suggests a volcano, but it is a skin outbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakout of spots on the skin is a skin eruption.

clue.text: Man soon set to build — builder!

indicators.note: to build is to put together, so the letters of man soon set are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A worker is about to start building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to build' rearranges MAN SOON SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who cuts and lays stone is one kind of builder.
